title: Vowel-shifted heading over a Latin poem, Ambrosiana A 118 inf. f. 154r (catalogue #1347)

documents.shelfmark: Milan, Biblioteca Ambrosiana, A 118 inf., unit 1, n. 6, f. 154r

transcription.source: Ambrosiana digital library IIIF, canvas 319 (1513 x 2000 px); catalogue OPAC incipit
transcription.notes: First glyph a ligature (OPAC reads m); seventh glyph r or x; minim letters ambiguous.

system.summary: Monoalphabetic vowel shift: each vowel written as the next letter (a>b, e>f, i>l, o>p, u>x), consonants unchanged; applied to one word of a heading.
system.notes: Inferred from the nine letters alone; too short to test statistically. The catalogue says only 'carme cifrato'. Only e, o, i are attested; a>b and u>x are assumed.

prior_solution.where: OPAC lists none; web searches on the incipit found nothing

conditions.human_role: Gave the catalogue number and asked for it to be solved and written up; no target-specific intervention.

solution.what: Fetched f. 154r from the Ambrosiana IIIF manifest (canvas 319).
Read the heading and transcribed the 16-line poem; the body is plain Latin, only the heading word is enciphered.
Vowel shift to the next letter (a>b, e>f, i>l, o>p, u>x) from the absence of a, i, u and the repeated f, p, l.
Undid the shift: ?-e-n-o-e-i-?-e-o with r or x in seventh place; also full Caesar +1 (no word).
Web searches on the incipit and lines of the poem; OPAC record read for an attribution.

outcome.method_basis: The vowel-shift mechanism fits the nine-letter heading word, but undoing it gives no Latin or Italian name, and the glyphs are ambiguous at the available image size.
outcome.notes: Needs the poem's attribution from other manuscripts or a better image of the heading.
